summary: Implemented file and virtual resources, explicitly encoded locations with deferred UTF-8/16/32 conversion against target text, workspace snapshots and root/symlink policy. Injected root and ignore services provide root discovery/canonicalization and one shared hidden/ignored/symlink policy snapshot. Canonical roots are cached by lexical alias and re-resolved on explicit refresh; tabs can retain independent workspaces, same-root attachment preserves generation, refresh advances generation, and removed or changed roots invalidate old identities. Ordered multi-root data is preserved but execution reports the planned single-root limit. Shared filesystem and search fixture files cover hidden entries, project and nested .gitignore, .ignore, include/exclude paths and explicit policy expectations. Files/Search filtering and parent/global ignore parity are not implemented by WB-04 and are documented as unavailable until WB-07/WB-09; no provider behavior is claimed.

gates.command: Review docs/CONTRACTS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/PLAN.md#wb-04, docs/PROVIDERS.md and the changed module dependency/lifetime inventory; run make check-ownership and git diff --check.
gates.result: WB-04 runtime ownership is limited to lua/workbench/core/{resource,location,workspace,root_policy}.lua and lua/workbench/services/workspace.lua; tests, fixtures, task documentation and evidence are under workbench-owned paths. Core imports no service/provider/UI code; the workspace service imports core modules only and receives root/ignore adapters explicitly. Plain model tables own no processes, timers, watchers, subscriptions, buffers or windows. The workspace service owns its workspace records, launch options and canonical-root cache; remove() releases the record/options/cache idempotently, and callers receive independent defensive snapshots. No command entrypoint, init.lua, host/Nix integration, external dependency or hosted CI was added.

All 17 mini.test cases passed on both Neovim 0.11.7 and 0.12.4 (16 WB-04 model cases plus the harness probe). Coverage includes escaped and invalid-byte file paths, virtual URIs, UTF-8/16/32 coordinate conversion after target text is supplied, emoji/surrogate boundaries, combining characters, CJK, tabs and CRLF, malformed ranges, root precedence, nested repositories, aliases, explicit folder scope, marker/cwd fallback, case-sensitive identities, containment boundaries, followed-symlink cycles/external targets, policy validation, shared fixture existence/policy equality, ordered multi-root snapshots and explicit unsupported capability state.

gates.command: Run make test; inspect the repeated-open/remove, root-refresh, alias-target-change and independent-workspace cases in tests/runtime/test_workspace_model.lua.
gates.result: One hundred distinct workspace open/remove cycles leave zero retained workspace records and no current old snapshot. Reopening an identical root for another consumer preserves its generation and canonicalizes only once; explicit refresh advances generation and rejects the old snapshot. If an alias resolves to a new canonical root, refresh invalidates/removes the previous identity; if canonicalization fails because the root vanished, the prior valid snapshot remains intact. Switching tabs/workspace IDs and removing one record does not invalidate a sibling workspace. No asynchronous callbacks or external handles are created by WB-04, so there are no late external emissions to leak.
